description:
src/backend.rs:626-646 — QueryCalendarEventsError::ExpandDurationTooLarge has
this doc:

    /// `expandRecurrences` was requested but `before - after` exceeds the
    /// account's `maxExpandedQueryDuration` capability (§5.11, §10.7.3).

But the trait has no method that exposes `maxExpandedQueryDuration` itself.
Backends cannot communicate the value to handlers, handlers cannot
communicate it to clients, and there's no place to put it in the JMAP
session capability response. The error variant exists to signal "you
exceeded a cap" but the cap value is invisible to everyone except the
backend's private state.

Workspace AGENTS.md "Backend caps and limits" section is explicit about the
canonical pattern for this:

    "Shape: fn limits(&self, caller: &Self::CallerCtx, account_id: &Id) -> XxxLimits —
     a sync default method on the extension's backend trait returning a
     struct of all related caps as a group. Each extension defines its
     own XxxLimits struct (e.g. ChatLimits, future CalendarsLimits)."

The same section explicitly anticipates this gap:

    "Precedent: ChatBackend::limits(&self, caller, account_id) -> ChatLimits
     (bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8)."

The canonical mail-server still uses the older per-method shape
(max_collapse_threads_emails, max_body_value_bytes, max_delayed_send_seconds
at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:296-347). That shape is documented
as the pre-standardisation pattern. Calendars has BOTH: no per-method
max_* methods and no limits() struct.

What goes wrong for the caller:

  1. A backend author writing a calendars impl with a real DB cannot tell
     handlers what their cap is; the only path to refuse a request is to
     return ExpandDurationTooLarge after attempting the query (or
     introspecting the filter range and short-circuiting based on the
     backend's PRIVATE state). There's no way for handlers to pre-check
     and reject without a backend round-trip.

  2. A consumer wanting to surface the cap to clients via JMAP session
     capability has nowhere to read it from. The server consumer has to
     duplicate the cap value into its session-capability builder out-of-band.

  3. The trait is forward-incompatible: when the canonical pattern propagates
     to mail-server (per workspace AGENTS.md), calendars will need to
     migrate too. Adopting it now (with sensible Default impls per the
     workspace's `XxxLimits` pattern) is non-breaking; bolting it on
     after a 0.x consumer base exists requires coordination.

Fix: add a CalendarsLimits struct (#[non_exhaustive], Default, conservative
reference defaults), and a default-method on CalendarsBackend:

    fn limits(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    ) -> CalendarsLimits {
        let _ = (caller, account_id);
        CalendarsLimits::default()
    }

Initial CalendarsLimits.max_expanded_query_duration backed by a sensible
default. Handler-side pre-check in query_calendar_events compares
`before - after` against the value before invoking the backend.

P2 — substantive design gap with a known-canonical fix; not a present-day bug.
title: CalendarsBackend lacks limits()/cap-advertising surface; maxExpandedQueryDuration referenced but unreachable
